patients.summary: Long-haul truck driver with type 2 diabetes since 2004, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and obesity who joined in 2018 on a fixed five-drug regimen. Over eight years outside letters add moderate obstructive sleep apnea, achalasia and cervical spondylotic myelopathy, none treated, while A1c drifts from the low 7s to 9.2. Chart ends shortly after an ED visit for a right vitreous hemorrhage, with ophthalmology records outstanding.

documents.title: New patient intake call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller: patient, calling from his truck (on a run through Ohio, back home this weekend).
Wants to establish primary care. Previous PCP retired this summer.
Says he has "sugar, pressure and cholesterol" and sees endocrinology and cardiology at outside groups already. Wants a doctor who will answer a text while he is on the road.
Membership agreement and fee schedule emailed to lamar.bryant@example.test. Records release form emailed for his prior primary care office; he will sign and send back.
New patient visit booked for 09/18, 8:40, first slot so he can leave by 10. Asked to bring all pill bottles and any lab printouts. Fasting not needed but he prefers to come fasting so labs can be drawn same day; ok per protocol.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

54-year-old man establishing care. Long-haul truck driver, usually out 10-12 days at a stretch, home 3-4 days. Married, lives in Chicopee. Came fasting.

Brings: type 2 diabetes since 2004 (diagnosed at about age 40), high blood pressure and high cholesterol, both treated for about as long as the diabetes. Follows with an outside endocrinology group for the diabetes and an outside cardiology group for blood pressure; plans to keep both. Wants us as home base, labs here when possible since our draw station opens early.

Current medications (bottles reviewed, all filled within the last 2 months):
- metformin 1000 mg twice daily with meals
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- amlodipine 5 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg every morning
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
Says he rarely misses a dose; keeps the pill organizer in the cab. Some days the evening metformin slips when he eats late.

Allergies: NKDA.
Surgical history: none.
Family history: father with type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure and sleep apnea. Mother with high blood pressure and high cholesterol. Paternal uncle with coronary artery disease.
Social: former smoker, about 20 pack-years, quit 03/2011. Alcohol 1-2 drinks a month. No other substances. Eats most meals at truck stops; tries to pick the grilled options "when they have them." No regular exercise.

ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no foot numbness or sores, no vision change, no urinary symptoms. Otherwise negative as asked.

Exam
BP 147/94, HR 69, RR 12, T 36.4, SpO2 97% RA. Wt 101.5 kg, Ht 178.2 cm, BMI 32.0.
Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart: regular rate and rhythm, S1 S2 normal, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, central adiposity. Extremities without edema.
Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers, DP and PT pulses 2+ bilaterally, 10 g monofilament felt at all sites tested both feet.
PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment / Plan
1. Type 2 diabetes, on metformin. A1c, BMP, CBC, urine albumin/creatinine today. Foot exam normal. Asked him to send us his last outside eye exam if he has one.
2. Essential hypertension on lisinopril, amlodipine and HCTZ. 147/94 today, above goal. First visit, rushed in from the parking lot; nurse BP recheck in about 4 weeks before deciding anything. He has a home cuff, will log a few morning readings.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipid panel today.
4. Obesity, BMI 32. Talked about truck-stop food choices and walking laps at fuel stops. He is skeptical but willing.
5. Former smoker, quit 2011, 20 pack-years. Not yet in a lung screening group by current criteria; revisit as guidelines change.
6. Health maintenance: flu shot today. One-time hepatitis C and HIV screening ordered, he agreed. Prior records requested for colonoscopy and immunization history. Shingles vaccine to discuss next visit.

Return: nurse BP check ~4 weeks; diabetes follow-up in January.

documents.title: Lab results reviewed

documents.body:
Results 09/18 reviewed.
A1c 7.1. Glucose 133 fasting. Creatinine 1.04, eGFR 85, potassium 4.2. Urine albumin/creatinine 11, normal.
Lipids: TC 201, HDL 40, TG 182, LDL 125.
CBC unremarkable (Hgb 14.5, WBC 7.9, plt 317).
HCV and HIV pending.
Portal message sent to patient. Continue current regimen; recheck A1c in January.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Mr. Bryant,

All of your results from Tuesday are back. Your hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Your A1c is 7.1, close to where we want it, and your kidney numbers and blood counts are normal. Your LDL ("bad") cholesterol is 125 on atorvastatin.

No changes for now. Keep sending me your home blood pressures when you have a few.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: thanks doc. got it. will send BP numbers when Im back from this run. parked in Joliet tonight

documents.title: Prior primary care records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior primary care office (42 pages), scanned to media.
Summary for PCP:
- Problem list there: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity (BMI 31-33 at their visits back to 2014). Same five medications and doses as our list.
- Screening colonoscopy 2014: normal, no polyps. Repeat interval 10 years noted.
- Tdap 05/12/2015. Added to immunization history.
- No pneumococcal, shingles or hepatitis B vaccines documented.
- No prior chest imaging on file.
Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Prior records reviewed. Colonoscopy 2014 normal; next colorectal screening due 2024. Tdap current through 2025. Health maintenance updated.

documents.title: Blood pressure check
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Nurse visit for BP recheck per PCP.
Seated 5 minutes, large adult cuff, left arm: 148/94, HR 65. Repeat after 3 minutes about the same.
Took all morning meds at 5 am including HCTZ, amlodipine and lisinopril.
Brought home log (his own cuff, mornings over the past two weeks): readings mostly mid-140s over about 90.
Denies headache, chest pain, vision change.
Routed to PCP.

documents.title: BP recheck review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed nurse BP and his home log: running 140s/90s on lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25. He is also followed by outside cardiology for BP, about once a year, and would rather any medication change come from them. Will hold off adjusting here for now and recheck at our January visit. Reinforced lower-salt choices on the road. Message sent.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Electronic refill request from retail pharmacy for metformin 1000 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, HCTZ 25 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg. Patient asked for 90-day supplies because of his road schedule.
Last visit 09/18, next visit 01/22 booked. Sent per refill protocol, 90 days with 1 refill each.

documents.title: Diabetes and Blood Pressure Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back from a run to Georgia last week. No complaints. Taking all five medicines; evening metformin still gets missed maybe once a week on long driving days. Home BP readings since October mostly 140-146 over 88-92, a few in the 130s. No chest pain, dyspnea, foot problems or vision change. Eating "a little better," fewer fried meals.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, HCTZ 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.

O: BP 143/90, HR 60, RR 15, T 36.5, SpO2 98%. Wt 101.1 kg, BMI 31.8.
Alert, comfortable. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. No ankle edema. Feet: intact skin, pulses palpable, monofilament normal.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes: A1c drawn today. Keep metformin 1000 BID. Suggested setting a phone alarm for the evening dose.
2. Hypertension: still running low 140s/90 on three agents. Again prefers to leave medication changes to his cardiologist. Will keep sending our readings. Salt and fast food talk again.
3. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 40, lipids in July.
4. Obesity: weight stable.
5. Shingrix dose 1 today, dose 2 in 2-6 months (July visit works).

Follow-up July, fasting labs that morning.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.4, fasting glucose 140. A bit above last fall. Portal note to patient: same plan, more consistent evening metformin and fewer sugary drinks on the road; recheck in July.

documents.title: Letter for DOT physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, my DOT medical card is up in April. The examiner at the clinic by the depot wants a note from my regular doctor saying my diabetes and blood pressure are under control and what meds Im on. Can you do that? I can pick it up Saturday or you can email it. Thanks Lamar

documents.title: Letter for commercial driver medical examiner
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the certified medical examiner:

Mr. Lamar Bryant (DOB 02/26/1964) is under my care for type 2 diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

His diabetes is treated with metformin 1000 mg twice daily. He does not use insulin. Most recent A1c 7.4% (01/2019). He has had no episodes of hypoglycemia.

His hypertension is treated with lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Office readings over the past six months have been in the 140s systolic and around 90 diastolic. He is also followed by cardiology.

Other medication: atorvastatin 40 mg daily.

Please contact the office with any questions.

documents.title: RE: Letter for DOT physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mr. Bryant, your letter is ready. A copy is attached here and the original will be at the front desk on Saturday morning.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sent both to your pharmacy in Chicopee this morning, 90-day supply. Safe driving.

documents.title: Diabetes and Blood Pressure Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here fasting for six-month check. Busy summer on the road, mostly the Midwest loop. Taking his medicines. Home BP "about the same," log forgotten in the truck. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no foot complaints. His DOT card was renewed this spring.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg.
NKDA.

Exam: BP 148/89, HR 55, RR 14, T 36.5, SpO2 97%. Weight 101.9 kg, BMI 32.1.
No distress. Cardiac exam regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Feet unchanged, sensation intact.

Assessment and plan
- T2DM: fasting labs drawn (A1c, BMP). Continue metformin.
- HTN: 148/89 here, still above goal on three drugs. He sees endocrinology later this month and cardiology this winter. Continue current doses; bring the log next time.
- Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today, on atorvastatin 40.
- Shingrix #2 given today; series complete.
- Annual physical in the fall.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Labs 07/16: fasting glucose 132, A1c 7.3, creatinine 1.0 (eGFR 89), K 4.0. TC 190, HDL 40, LDL 120, TG 150.
Stable. Will send to his endocrinologist ahead of his visit, per his request. No changes.

documents.title: Endocrinology office note
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY — OUTPATIENT NOTE
Visit date: 07/29/2019
Patient: Lamar Bryant, 55-year-old man
Copy to: primary care

Reason for visit: scheduled diabetes review.

History: Type 2 diabetes for about 15 years, also on treatment for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He has no acute concerns today. He does say that for the last few months he has felt more worn out than usual. He has not had chest pain or palpitations, and he denies increased thirst, increased urination or weight loss he was not trying for.

Medications as reported: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; also takes lisinopril for blood pressure.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and sleep apnea; mother with hypertension and hyperlipidemia; paternal uncle with coronary disease.
Social: drives long-haul. Former smoker, 20 pack-years, stopped about 8 years ago. Alcohol 1-2 drinks per month.

Exam: BP 138/86. BMI 32. General exam otherwise without abnormal findings.

Data (drawn by his primary care office 07/16/2019): fasting glucose 132 mg/dL; total cholesterol 190, HDL 40, LDL 120, triglycerides 150 mg/dL; creatinine 1.0 mg/dL.

Impression: Type 2 diabetes on metformin monotherapy, metabolic labs as above.
Plan: No changes to his regimen today. Continue current medications.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
DIABETIC EYE EXAMINATION — REPORT TO PRIMARY CARE
Exam date: 08/14/2019
Patient: Lamar Bryant

Dilated fundus examination, both eyes.
Visual acuity with correction: 20/20 right, 20/20 left.
Intraocular pressures normal both eyes.
Lens: clear.
Optic nerves: healthy rim, cup-to-disc 0.3 both eyes.
Macula: flat, normal foveal reflex both eyes.
Vessels and periphery: no hemorrhages, no microaneurysms, no exudates, no neovascularization.

Impression: No diabetic retinopathy either eye.
Recommendation: repeat dilated exam in 1-2 years.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Lamar is 55, here fasting. Doing ok. Says the endocrinology visit in July was routine, no changes. Some long weeks on the road this fall. No new symptoms today.

PMH: type 2 diabetes (2004), hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; HCTZ 25 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: none.
FH: father T2DM, HTN, OSA; mother HTN, HLD; paternal uncle CAD.
SH: married, Chicopee. Long-haul driver. Former smoker, quit 03/2011, 20 pack-years. 1-2 drinks/month.

ROS negative except as above.

Vitals: BP 145/89, HR 80, RR 14, T 36.6, SpO2 96%. Wt 101.7 kg, Ht 178.6 cm, BMI 31.9.
General: well, no distress.
Eyes: conjunctivae clear. Ears: canals clear, TMs normal. Mouth: moist, dentition fair.
Neck: no adenopathy or thyromegaly.
CV: regular, no murmurs. Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, nontender, no masses.
GU: deferred, patient preference.
Skin: no rashes. Ext: no edema.
Feet: skin intact, nails trimmed, pedal pulses 2+, monofilament intact bilaterally.
Neuro: grossly normal, gait normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment / Plan
- Health maintenance: flu vaccine today. Hepatitis B series recommended for adults with diabetes under 60; Heplisav-B dose 1 today, dose 2 in one month. Shingrix complete. Tdap 2015. Colonoscopy 2014 normal, due 2024. Eye exam 08/2019 without retinopathy.
- PSA: discussed benefits and harms of screening, including higher baseline risk for Black men. He wants it checked. PSA drawn.
- T2DM: A1c 7.3 in July. BMP and urine albumin/creatinine today. Diabetic foot exam normal.
- HTN: 145/89. Remains above goal on three agents. Cardiology visit is coming in January; he will ask them. Continue for now.
- Hyperlipidemia: LDL 120 in July; continue atorvastatin 40.
- Obesity: BMI ~32, stable.
CBC with today's labs. RTC January for diabetes follow-up; RN visit in 4 weeks for hep B #2.
